id./param/talk_party/talk_party_a080.pack|t: What's wrong, {var:1}? To chase the merchant with the Rainbough, our only way is to cross the sea by ship.
If we dawdle, we won't get the branch. Let's hurry back to Gondolia and get the mayor to open the dock.
Gondolia seems big on trade, so I was hoping to find some lovely shoes in my size...
...No luck. Everything's childish. I thought getting younger was all upside, but fashion is surprisingly hard.
To tell the truth, I bought my darling ship on a whim long ago. Never thought it'd come in handy like this.
My darling ship is a bit old, but I keep her well maintained, so you can feel completely safe aboard.
I don't know who cursed an innocent child, but when I find them I'll pound them to a pulp!
Come on, {var:1}, let's hurry. First we find the pretty spring in the cave west of Gondolia!
I believe songbird nectar can lift the curse, but making it needs holy water from a pure spring.
Oh, leave making the songbird nectar to me. I know a little about mixing medicine.
Serena says that, but she's not someone who'd go down that easily.
...Right, Erik?
Looks like Veronica and Serena went off with Sylvando too. What a restless bunch.
Well, grumbling won't help. Let's go to the mayor's house northeast of town and somehow get the dock opened.
When she snatched Veronica's wand at first, I took her for a kid thief...
If he stole out of desperation for a friend, it'd be sad to stay angry. Let's find a way to help.
The curse on the boy Placido was cast by very powerful magic. Who would do something so cruel...
That boy's eyes looked so pained. Let's make him able to speak cheerfully again as soon as we can.
{var:1} darling, I heard everything! You're headed to the cave west of Gondolia to save the boy!
Hmph, my ears pick up cries for help anywhere. Let's go!
Suddenly deciding to save a kid, then telling us to claim seats when we get back... Those two are so self-willed.
Annoying, but it can't be helped. Let's go see the stage, just for a look.
That officer is so short-tempered. We must hurry or Erik is in danger, but charging in head-on is a bad bet.
I recall a passage from the northwest gondola landing around behind the stage. Let's go that way and approach.
Take a gondola along the town canal and we should reach behind the stage. Now, let's rescue Erik!
How many Heliodor soldiers are staked out in Gondolia? There seem to be a lot.
If we fight them all, we'll run out of stamina. Let's find a path where the soldiers won't see us.
Oh, Master Erik. I hope that general hasn't been rough with him...
I share the blame for Master Erik being captured. I must save him somehow...
The town is full of soldiers. But if we move through the buildings, we can avoid pointless fights.
First, let's scout Erik from the bridge in the middle of town! Then the counterattack begins!
After that commotion I was worried about coming back, but the mayor seems to have explained things to everyone.
Some Heliodor soldiers are in town, but they haven't noticed you're the Luminary. They look like rookies.
Alice is my best apprentice. Even if we leave town, she looks after the Sylvando for us. Such a good girl.
While we're off the ship, she keeps watch so no mischief-makers touch it, so don't worry.
We spent all that time in Gallopolis with desert as far as the eye could see... I get wanting to visit places with water.
But {var:1}, remember the Rainbough we're after too, once you've had your fill.
...Speaking of which, even before I met you, Serena wandered everywhere and got us lost in strange places like this.
Our next destination is Gondolia. I'll just say that much, so head to town once you're satisfied.
Ah... I'm so happy there's so much water here. In Gallopolis I was always covered in sand.
By the way, {var:1}, are you perhaps lost? Oh, I hope I'm mistaken.
Oh my, {var:1} darling. I was wondering when to say it, but we've already passed Gondolia.
Knowing where you are is very important when traveling, so be careful. First, let's look at the map again!
The river flowing through this cave leads toward Gondolia... It seems to be a headwater that runs to the sea.
If we go deeper into the cave, there should surely be a place where clear water wells up. Let's follow the stream.
The songbird nectar that cures Placido's voice can be made from the pure spring in this cave, right?
Serena will make the songbird nectar, so let's first aim for the pure spring!
We're too nice, aren't we? Wanted men helping people.
Let's wrap up this trouble fast. Then we'll board the ship and hunt for the Rainbough.
Songbird nectar... how nostalgic.
Dissolve songbird nectar in hot water and drink it, and your throat feels much better. We drank it often as kids.
Songbird nectar is a medicine from the holy land of Arboria. A bard with a sore throat who drank it regained a lovely voice.
If the boy with the cursed throat drinks the nectar, he should speak again. His voice may even be lovelier than before.
Now the boy's throat curse can be lifted. Let's hurry and deliver the nectar to Gondolia.
The Mighty Man Contest should be starting too. I'd like him to enjoy it with his throat healed.
Wait, {var:1}! Erik is a hostage, and you're out here cooling off?!
Who knows what they'll do to him if we leave him like that. Let's hurry back to Gondolia!
{var:1}, I like walks too, but I can't enjoy myself while Master Erik suffers.
If you've forgotten something, I'll go along. When you're ready, let's return to Gondolia, where Master Erik is held.
Could it be, {var:1}... that you came here to train because you worry you can't save Erik as you are?
In that case I'll go along. If we fall together with Erik, we'd all be caught.
Are you the type who keeps returning to caves where your business is long done?
Well, I was a thief myself, so I get the feeling. All right, let's see if any treasure is left.
It's quiet here with few people, and the dim light is calming. This is a lovely cave, to my taste.
Now that we have a ship, we can visit all sorts of caves and towers. Hee hee, I'm getting excited.
If you sing in a narrow rocky place like this, your voice echoes and you feel a little better at singing!
I suddenly feel like singing. La-la-la, our dear Luminary {var:1}! Our Luminary darling!
This sea breeze... the endlessly blue ocean... Scenes like this remind me of growing up by the sea as a kid.
...No, I'm rambling. Now, let's head for Bandelfon, where the merchant with the Rainbough went.
My home, the holy land of Arboria, is deep in the mountains. I saw the sea for the first time only after setting out to find you.
Mountains give me energy, but looking at the sea feels like washing away my doubts and weakness.
Ugh... a passing seagull snatched the sweets I bought in Gondolia when I tried to eat them...
I thought I'd finally catch my breath after escaping General Jasper, but I was naive...
Sweet naivety...
Hee hee, {var:1} darling, how do you like the ride on my Sylvando?
I do worry she looks a bit plain, but I like her current design too, so I can't decide whether to give her a makeover.
I grew up deep in the mountains, so people always worried I'd start a forest fire if I practiced magic too much.
If I'd been born somewhere like this, I could blast Frizz or anything at the sea. Ugh, now I really want to.
...Oh, sorry, I wasn't listening. Listening to the ripples made me sleepy...
...Say, {var:1} darling. This isn't where the merchant with the Rainbough went, is it?
I understand wanting to stop at unfamiliar lands, but let's hurry to Bandelfon.
Both are seaside towns, but Gondolia and Puerto Valor feel quite different. This is what you'd call a resort town...
Speaking of which, I hear Puerto Valor has a casino. Why not try it for a change of pace?
Hmm, a lot of wealthy people seem to live in Puerto Valor. You can tell from the layout of the town.
I can see why rich people would want to keep a view like this to themselves every day.
Are you looking for Sylvando? Just as we reached the town entrance, she went outside to pick flowers.
Now that you mention it, lovely flowers were blooming outside town. Sylvando must like flowers.
Oh, a casino! You look serious, but you like places like this after all.
We're always hunted and never rest, so playing to relax once in a while might be good.
A casino is a fine social club for ladies and gentlemen... so said a book in Arboria. So this is a casino.
But it's noisy and the flashing decorations hurt my eyes... I think the forest of Arboria suits me better.
...Oh, {var:1}, what is it? Sorry, the coins are so loud I couldn't hear a thing.
What are you doing here now? Coming back so boldly, want to eat that awful food again?
With flashy Sylvando here we stand out. Let's get out quickly.
{var:1}, I understand wanting to storm the castle and clear up the misunderstanding, but now is not the time.
Don't rush. Let's head for Yggdrasil. Surely the misunderstanding will clear someday.
So this is Heliodor, the kingdom that drove {var:1} out as the Darkspawn...
Everyone in this kingdom seems nice, so why did they start calling {var:1} the Darkspawn?
This place has no small connection to me too.
But that's another story. Hee hee.
How long has it been since we left here together? Nothing has changed since then.
...Hey, {var:1}. It hurts, but all we can do is move forward. Let's not look back.
You can stay here a while. All we can do is be by your side...
How awful... just because you're the Luminary, they did this to {var:1}'s home...
...I can't forgive you, Heliodor!
I was ready for this ever since we escaped Heliodor Castle together, but... they beat us here.
We can't let our guard down from here on. Stay sharp, {var:1}.
Keep detours moderate, and let's hunt for the merchant with the Rainbough.
According to Alice, the merchant went to Bandelfon, northeast of Gondolia. Let's take the ship after him.
Oh, sorry. I was thinking about the cake I ate in Gondolia...
{var:1} darling isn't traveling just to clear the Darkspawn name, but still...
It's a blessing to have people like Mayor Rotondo who understand {var:1} darling.
Honestly, being chased all over Gondolia by Jasper was awful.
He was furious at being outwitted, so he'll be even more persistent now. That's the grudge-holding type.
Gathering so many soldiers to catch {var:1}. Heliodor really means it.
Then we'll just defend with all we've got. I'll protect {var:1}, Veronica, so don't worry.
...But you're surprisingly spacey, which worries me. Do your part and try to be protected.
The merchant who bought the Rainbough went to Bandelfon... Alice said so, right?
We still have little information. Let's just visit many places. Maybe we'll learn something.
Make everyone in the world smile... that's my goal, so I've traveled many places as an entertainer.
What I learned on those travels: when you arrive somewhere new, first listen to the people who live there!
Oh right, north of the Dundrasil region there should be a big town where people gather. Let's gather information there.
I usually travel alone or in a pair. This is my first time with such a big group.
It's a bit conspicuous for fugitives, but sneaking around all the time is tiring, and I don't mind lively company.
...Though one of us is a bit too lively for a kid. If we watch out for her, it's fine.
H-hey, {var:1}. Walk more slowly, please.
I'm in a kid's body now, so my stride is different from yours. I've been speed-walking and I'm tired.
I wonder if the Rainbough really shines in rainbow colors, like its name. Either way, we still lack information.
Oh right, north of the Dundrasil region there should be a big town where people gather. Let's gather information there.
So this is Grotto. I heard it's a fighting town with an arena, and there really are lots of fighters.
But what's a masked martial arts tournament? Let's go take a look, {var:1}.
Wow, look, {var:1}! A whole town is inside this big building!
The whole town is like a giant fortress! With no rain, you needn't worry about wet laundry.
But why does this town display such a huge statue of General Hendrik?
Did he help the town somehow? Still, it shows Hendrik is a hero loved by everyone.
